# Introduction & Course Organisation

## Course organisation {#slide-2}

- Lecturers: Prof. Dr. Matthias Kalverkamp & Prof. Dr. Thomas Kirschstein
- Documents + materials: https://github.com/tkirschstein/SCM
- Case studies: 6 case studies in group work 3-6 persons
- Exam: reflection report

## Literature {#slide-3}


::: {#refs}
:::

## Structure of the lecture {#slide-4}

1.  Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management
2.  Strategic Design of Supply Chains
3.  Uncertainty and Risk Management in Supply Chains


# Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management

## Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management {#slide-5}

- **Tasks, terms and concepts**
- Objectives & trade-offs
- Costs & management

## Learning objectives {#learning-objectives-introduction}

After this unit you will be able to …

- **explain** key terms, actors and flows of a supply chain,
- **distinguish** supply chain management from logistics and procurement,
- **differentiate** between strategic, tactical and operational decisions in supply chains,
- **assess** the importance of coordination for value creation and competitiveness.

**Further reading**

- **SCM fundamentals and decision levels:** Chapters 1–3 in [@chopra2025supply].
- **Strategies, instruments and controlling in the German-speaking context:** Chapters 1–3 in [@werner2020supply].
- **Case-oriented introduction to supply chain structures:** Chapters 1–3 in [@sople2011supply].

## Supply chains in History {#slide-6}

::: slide-subtitle
Cheops and building supply chains
:::

- Cheops pyramid building started about 2620 BC, ancient height: 147 m
- 2.3 million stone blocks, avg. 2.5 t each
- Required coordinated transport, tool inventory, and mass catering for about 100,000 workers

::: {layout-ncol="2"}

![](images/image7.png)
:::

## Supply chains in History {#slide-7}

::: slide-subtitle
Hannibal's invasion of Italy
:::

- Invasion from Spain to Italy in the 2nd Punic War\
- 37 war elephants + 40,000 troops (incl. large cavalry)
- Supply of troops and beasts had to be realised in hostile territory

### Raw material and sales map

```{r}
library(leaflet)
library(htmltools)
library(sf)
library(jsonlite)

sichtbare_punkte <- data.frame(
  name = c("Taranto", "Ostia", "Rome", "Tyre", "Miletus"),
  rolle = c("Sheep's wool", "Receiving port", "Further processing and sales", "Purple dye", "Sheep's wool"),
  lat = c(40.4644, 41.7440, 41.8933, 33.2704, 37.5300),
  lng = c(17.2470, 12.2500, 12.4829, 35.2038, 27.2800),
  color = c("#2a6f97", "#b8860b", "#b8860b", "#7a3ea1", "#2a6f97")
)

osrm_route_sf <- function(coords, color, label) {
  coords <- as.matrix(coords)
  if (!is.numeric(coords)) stop("coords must be numeric.")
  if (ncol(coords) != 2) stop("coords must have exactly 2 columns: lon, lat.")
  if (anyNA(coords)) stop("coords contains NA values. Please check coordinates.")

  coord_string <- paste(
    apply(coords, 1, function(x) sprintf("%.6f,%.6f", x[1], x[2])),
    collapse = ";"
  )

  url <- paste0(
    "https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1/driving/",
    coord_string,
    "?overview=full&geometries=geojson&steps=false"
  )

  js <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url)
  line <- sf::st_linestring(as.matrix(js$routes$geometry$coordinates[[1]]))
  sf::st_sf(label = label, color = color, geometry = sf::st_sfc(line, crs = 4326))
}

manual_route_sf <- function(coords, color, label) {
  sf::st_sf(
    label = label,
    color = color,
    geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_linestring(as.matrix(coords)), crs = 4326)
  )
}

route_tarent_rom <- osrm_route_sf(
  coords = matrix(c(
    17.2470, 40.4644,
    12.4829, 41.8933
  ), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 2),
  color = "#2a6f97",
  label = "Taranto → Rome: OSRM-based land route"
)

route_milet_ostia <- manual_route_sf(
  matrix(c(
    27.2800, 37.5300,  # Miletus
    24.8093, 35.2401,  # Crete (waypoint only)
    15.5540, 38.1938,  # Messina (waypoint only)
    12.2500, 41.7440   # Ostia
  ), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 2),
  color = "#2a6f97",
  label = "Miletus → Crete → Messina → Ostia: sea route"
)

route_tyros_ostia <- manual_route_sf(
  matrix(c(
    35.2038, 33.2704,  # Tyre
    24.8093, 35.2401,  # Crete (waypoint only)
    15.5540, 38.1938,  # Messina (waypoint only)
    12.2500, 41.7440   # Ostia
  ), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 2),
  color = "#7a3ea1",
  label = "Tyre → Crete → Messina → Ostia: sea route"
)

route_ostia_rom <- manual_route_sf(
  matrix(c(
    12.2500, 41.7440,
    12.4829, 41.8933
  ), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 2),
  color = "#b8860b",
  label = "Ostia → Rome: onward transport"
)

leaflet(width = "100%", height = "480px", options = leafletOptions(zoomControl = TRUE, dragging = TRUE)) |>
  addTiles(
    urlTemplate = "https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
    attribution = "&copy; <a href='https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright'>OpenStreetMap</a> contributors"
  ) |>
  setView(lng = 19.5, lat = 38.0, zoom = 5) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    data = sichtbare_punkte,
    lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat,
    radius = 6,
    color = ~color,
    weight = 2,
    fillColor = ~color,
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    popup = ~paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>", rolle)
  ) |>
  addPolylines(
    data = route_tarent_rom,
    color = "#2a6f97",
    weight = 3,
    opacity = 0.85,
    dashArray = "5,5",
    popup = ~label
  ) |>
  addPolylines(
    data = route_milet_ostia,
    color = "#2a6f97",
    weight = 4,
    opacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~label
  ) |>
  addPolylines(
    data = route_tyros_ostia,
    color = "#7a3ea1",
    weight = 4,
    opacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~label
  ) |>
  addPolylines(
    data = route_ostia_rom,
    color = "#b8860b",
    weight = 3,
    opacity = 0.9,
    dashArray = "6,6",
    popup = ~label
  ) |>
  addControl(
    html = HTML(paste0(
      "<div style='background:rgba(255,255,255,0.94);padding:8px 10px;",
      "border:1px solid #bbb;border-radius:8px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.4;'>",
      "<div style='margin-bottom:4px;'><b>Route legend</b></div>",
      "<div><span style='display:inline-block;width:18px;height:0;border-top:3px dashed #2a6f97;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle'></span>Taranto → Rome: land route</div>",
      "<div><span style='display:inline-block;width:18px;height:3px;background:#2a6f97;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle'></span>Miletus → Ostia: sea route</div>",
      "<div><span style='display:inline-block;width:18px;height:3px;background:#7a3ea1;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle'></span>Tyre → Ostia: sea route</div>",

      "</div>"
    )),
    position = "bottomright"
  )
```

```{r}
fig <- plot_ly()
legend_done <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
for (r in routes) {
  mat <- do.call(rbind, r$coords)
  lg <- paste(r$period, r$mode)
  show_leg <- if (!exists(lg, envir = legend_done, inherits = FALSE)) { assign(lg, TRUE, envir = legend_done); TRUE } else FALSE
  line_style <- if (r$mode == 'Caravan') list(color='#8c510a', width=2, dash='dot') else if (r$mode == 'Land route') list(color='#5f5f5f', width=2.5, dash='dash') else if (r$period == 'Before 1498') list(color='#8c510a', width=3) else list(color='#01696f', width=3)
  fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
    type='scattermapbox', mode='lines', lon=mat[,1], lat=mat[,2],
    line=line_style, name=lg, legendgroup=lg, showlegend=show_leg,
    hoverinfo='text', text=r$name
  )
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

# Uniform comparison in g silver per kg pepper
prices <- tribble(
  ~route, ~stage, ~value,
  "Before 1498", "Moluccas", 1.5,
  "Before 1498", "Malacca", 4,
  "Before 1498", "Calicut", 8,
  "Before 1498", "Alexandria", 12.0,
  "Before 1498", "Venice", 16.0,
  "Before 1498", "European consumer markets", 25.0,
)

stage_order <- c(
  "Moluccas",
  "Malacca",
  "Calicut",
  "Alexandria",
  "Venice",
  "European consumer markets"
)

prices_plot <- prices %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_order))

p1 <- ggplot(prices_plot, aes(x = stage, y = value, fill = route)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 1)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Before 1498" = "#8c510a", "After 1498" = "#01696f")) +
  labs(
    title = "Price levels in the spice trade in silver equivalents",
    subtitle = "g silver per kg pepper",
    x = NULL,
    y = "g silver per kg"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))

p1
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

silver_per_maravedi <- 3.195 / 34

costs <- tribble(
  ~Schritt, ~Maravedis, ~Typ,
  "Ships, rigging, artillery, arms", -3912241, "Costs",
  "Provisions and barrels", -1585551, "Costs",
  "Wages for 237 persons", -1154504, "Costs",
  "Barter and trade goods", -1679769, "Costs",
  "Other requirements", -415060, "Costs",
  "Revenue from clove cargo", 7888684, "Revenue",
  "Other goods", 1000000, "Revenue"
) %>%
  mutate(
    Silber_g = Maravedis * silver_per_maravedi,
    Silber_kg = Silber_g / 1000
  )



waterfall <- costs %>%
  mutate(
    end = cumsum(Silber_kg),
    start = lag(end, default = 0)
  )

p <- ggplot(waterfall) +
  geom_rect(aes(
    xmin = seq_along(Schritt) - 0.35,
    xmax = seq_along(Schritt) + 0.35,
    ymin = pmin(start, end),
    ymax = pmax(start, end),
    fill = Typ
  )) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(aes(
    x = seq_along(Schritt),
    y = ifelse(Silber_kg < 0, end - 35, end + 35),
    label = round(Silber_kg, 1)
  ), size = 3.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(waterfall$Schritt), labels = waterfall$Schritt) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Costs" = "#b2182b", "Revenue" = "#1b7837")) +
  labs(
    title = "Economic balance of the Magellan expedition",
    subtitle = "Costs and revenues in kg silver equivalent",
    x = NULL,
    y = "kg silver equivalent",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))

p
```

Network concept & basic paradigm

```{dot}
//| fig-width: 13
//| fig-height: 3.5
//| out-width: 96%

digraph scn_network {

  graph [
    rankdir = LR,
    splines = curved,
    nodesep = 0.55,
    ranksep = 1.1,
    pad = 0.15,
    bgcolor = "transparent"
  ]

  node [
    shape = box,
    style = filled,
    fillcolor = "white",
    color = "black",
    penwidth = 1.1,
    fontname = "Arial",
    fontsize = 14,
    width = 1.9,
    height = 0.65
  ]

  edge [
    color = "black",
    penwidth = 1.1,
    arrowhead = normal,
    arrowsize = 0.8
  ]

  // Nodes per stage (column) and actor (row)
  s1 [label = "Supplier"];     s2 [label = "Supplier"];     s3 [label = "Supplier"];
  m1 [label = "Manufacturer"]; m2 [label = "Manufacturer"]; m3 [label = "Manufacturer"];
  d1 [label = "Distributor"];  d2 [label = "Distributor"];  d3 [label = "Distributor"];
  r1 [label = "Retailer"];     r2 [label = "Retailer"];     r3 [label = "Retailer"];
  c1 [label = "Consumer"];     c2 [label = "Consumer"];     c3 [label = "Consumer"];

  // common ranks per stage (column)
  { rank = same; s1; s2; s3 }
  { rank = same; m1; m2; m3 }
  { rank = same; d1; d2; d3 }
  { rank = same; r1; r2; r3 }
  { rank = same; c1; c2; c3 }

  // enforce vertical order within each stage
  s1 -> s2 -> s3 [style = invis, weight = 20]
  m1 -> m2 -> m3 [style = invis, weight = 20]
  d1 -> d2 -> d3 [style = invis, weight = 20]
  r1 -> r2 -> r3 [style = invis, weight = 20]
  c1 -> c2 -> c3 [style = invis, weight = 20]

  // Horizontal base connections (same row)
  s1 -> m1 [weight = 10]
  s2 -> m2 [weight = 10]
  s3 -> m3 [weight = 10]

  m1 -> d1 [weight = 10]
  m2 -> d2 [weight = 10]
  m3 -> d3 [weight = 10]

  d1 -> r1 [weight = 10]
  d2 -> r2 [weight = 10]
  d3 -> r3 [weight = 10]

  r1 -> c1 [weight = 10]
  r2 -> c2 [weight = 10]
  r3 -> c3 [weight = 10]

  // Cross-links between adjacent rows: Supplier -> Manufacturer
  s1 -> m2
  s2 -> m1
  s2 -> m3
  s3 -> m2

  // Cross-links: Manufacturer -> Distributor
  m1 -> d2
  m2 -> d1
  m2 -> d3
  m3 -> d2

  // Cross-links: Distributor -> Retailer
  d1 -> r2
  d2 -> r1
  d2 -> r3
  d3 -> r2

  // Cross-links: Retailer -> Consumer
  r1 -> c2
  r2 -> c1
  r2 -> c3
  r3 -> c2

  // outer arcs: first and last row each fully connected (Supplier <-> Consumer)
  //s1 -> c1 //[constraint = true]
  //s1 -> c2 [constraint = false]
  //s1 -> c3 [constraint = false]
  //s2 -> c1 [constraint = false]
  //s2 -> c3 [constraint = false]
  //s3 -> c1 [constraint = false]
  //s3 -> c2 [constraint = false]
  //s3 -> c3 //[constraint = true]
}
```

SCM profit = customer revenue -- total costs of all processes/partners = sum of indiv. profits

. . .

$\rightarrow$ **Optimising indiv. profits does not, as a rule, optimise the SCM profit!**

## Definitions of SCM {#slide-13}

::: slide-subtitle
Diversity & common core
:::

::: small-text
[@stadtler2000supply, p. 9]: "*Supply chain management is the task of integrating organisational units along the supply chain, coordinating the flows of materials, information and money, and improving the competitiveness of the entire supply chain in order to meet customer needs*." <br><br> [@hugos2018essentials]: “*Supply Chain Management is coordination of production , inventory , location , transportation , and information among the participants in a supply chain to achieve the best mix of responsiveness and efficiency for the market being served .*" <br><br> [@cscmp_definition]: “*Supply chain management encompasses the planning and management of all activities involved in sourcing and procurement, conversion, and all logistics management activities. Importantly, it also includes coordination and collaboration with channel partners, which can be suppliers, intermediaries, third party service providers, and customers. In essence, supply chain management integrates supply and demand management within and across companies .*"
:::

[@kummer2018grundzuge]

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Dispositive level**: covers the information flow within and between companies, planning processes, decision-making and control (management in the narrow sense)
- **Financial level**: covers money and payment flows within and outside the company
- **Goods level**: covers the movement and stock of physical goods (raw materials, auxiliary materials and supplies) within and between companies
:::

## Supply chain structures {#slide-16}

::: slide-subtitle
Focal supply chain
:::

![](images/clipboard-1428622780.png){fig-align="center" width="2428"}

::: small-text
**Characteristics**:

- Focal company in the bottleneck position → “controls” the network (actors and structure)
- High market power → controls market access
- Often the coordinator → sets standards and strategic objectives
- Examples: automotive industry, Apple, ...
:::

## Supply chain structures {#slide-17}

::: slide-subtitle
Polycentric supply chains
:::

![](images/clipboard-574717847.png){fig-align="center" width="2600"}

::: small-text
**Characteristics**:

- Distributed and overlapping competences
- Specialisation and cooperation
- No clear standardisation and a rather egalitarian distribution of market power
- Examples: IKEA, Neste, Unilever, ...
:::
